Will is a 58-year-old man living in Epalinges, an urban community near Lausanne, where he resides in a spacious 160 m² terraced house with three other adults. With a Bachelor’s degree and part-time employment, he shares his home with a household of working adults—none of whom are children—creating a dynamic suited to mutual independence and shared responsibilities. The four-room home accommodates their busy yet coordinated lifestyles, reflecting a balance between personal space and collective living.

On weekdays, Will rises early at 5 a.m., often beginning his day with quiet household tasks before the others stir. His part-time work allows flexibility, so he typically spends mornings on his laptop, handling professional duties or personal projects from home. Around mid-morning, he takes a break to wash the dishes, a chore he has naturally adopted as part of his routine. Lunch is a simple, home-prepared meal, eaten between tasks rather than during a fixed break, allowing him to make the most of his unstructured work hours.

Evenings follow a steadier rhythm: Will usually returns home by 6 p.m., and not long after, he prepares dinner for the household. Cooking serves as both a practical task and a way to unwind, often completed by early evening. After the meal, he spends time watching television or browsing on his laptop, a window of leisure that bridges the gap between day and night. By 9 p.m., he retires, valuing a full night’s rest to maintain his energy for the day ahead.

Weekends introduce a more relaxed pace. Will sleeps in when he can, though he still dedicates time to chores like cleaning and laundry, fitting them in around the household’s needs. His afternoons and evenings are often reserved for leisure, with extended periods spent watching films or using his laptop between 2 p.m. and 9 p.m. This flexibility extends to meal times, where cooking and eating align with the mood and plans of the day rather than a strict timetable.

In terms of habits, Will maintains regular eating patterns, typically consuming three homemade meals per day and rarely dining out. He is pragmatic about home comfort as well—fairly flexible with adjusting the heating by a degree or two to save energy or suit the moment, a small but telling detail of his adaptable and considerate nature.

Evenings find Xavier returning home, where she shifts focus to household management. As the sole occupant of her household, she maintains an independent and structured lifestyle, with no children or other adults sharing her space. Her home, compact yet comfortable, suits her needs as an older adult who values both routine and her proximity to the city’s amenities.

On weekdays, Kelly rises at 7:00 and begins her morning with a period of leisure, often watching television or using her laptop. By 9:00, she transitions to working at her desktop computer, dedicating an hour to personal projects, correspondence, or continued learning. Her mornings also include light cleaning around 10:00, followed by preparing and eating lunch near midday. Laundry is typically attended to in the late morning, fitting flexibly within her schedule before her second computer session in the late afternoon.

Evenings find Kelly at home, where she prepares dinner around 18:00 and later watches television or browses online. She maintains a tidy home, with another cleaning session around 15:00 and dishwashing completed after her evening meal. By 22:00, she retires for the night, ensuring she is well-rested for the day ahead. Kelly’s home occupancy is highest during these evening and late morning hours, reflecting her preference for a calm, home-centered lifestyle.

Weekends offer a slight variation in Kelly’s routine. She allows herself to sleep in until 7:00, though she stays up slightly later the night before. Meal times shift slightly, with lunch prepared closer to midday and dinner in the early evening. Her leisure and computer use are more concentrated in the later hours, and chores like laundry and dishwashing are handled at varying times, granting her a more relaxed pace. This flexibility extends to her heating preferences, as she is willing to adjust the temperature by a degree or two for comfort or energy savings.

Kelly’s eating habits are consistent and home-based, with three meals prepared daily in her own kitchen. She rarely eats out, preferring the rhythm of cooking at regular intervals—lunch around noon and dinner in the early evening. This regularity, combined with her structured yet adaptable approach to household management, defines a life of thoughtful independence and intellectual engagement in her later years.
